article_content: Environmental activist Rob Greenfield from San Diego, California, has begun living in a 50-square-foot (5ft x 10ft) mobile home to reduce expenses and embrace sustainable living. The 28-year-old purchased the compact dwelling for $950 after leaving his previous $1,600/month apartment. The space features a rocket stove, sleeping area, and reading nook. Greenfield seeks a permanent location to install solar panels, collect rainwater, and maintain a compost system. He proposes exchanging gardening services and homegrown produce with hosts who accommodate his mobile unit, while eschewing modern utilities. 'This demonstrates Earth-friendly living through radical simplicity,' Greenfield explained, highlighting his commitment to off-grid sustainability using bicycle transportation and community resource sharing.

article_content: A photograph documents a striped marlin hunting near Mexico's Baja California peninsula. The fish used its elongated snout at 50mph to isolate a sardine from a dispersed shoal. Marine photographer Doug Perrine captured this rare predatory behavior while free diving. Striped marlins typically slash or swallow prey whole, making this impaling action exceptional to record. Perrine highlights these apex predators' ecological significance and conservation threats from overfishing. While his close-range photography involves risk, he cautions against viewing it as endorsement for unsafe practices.
